source: SPM Study Bundle · Unforgettable Travel – Pulau Redang (Article 04) · Article, 200–250 words
paragraphs: The most unforgettable place I have ever visited is the gem of the South China Sea: Pulau Redang. This island is a safe place of pristine beaches and crystal-clear waters, far removed from the urban clamour. Redang is blessed with a lively sea life, making it a paradise for nature lovers, and the sand on Pasir Panjang is so extremely white it truly feels like walking on flour.

What made the trip special was the profound sense of tranquility it offered. I spent three days immersed in nature. My favourite activity was snorkelling over the underwater reefs, where the water visibility was so exceptional I felt like I was floating through an aquarium. I encountered schools of brightly coloured fish and giant sea turtles, a truly awe-inspiring sight. Furthermore, the isolation of the island forced me to unplug from digital devices and appreciate the amazing beauty of nature. This escape brought inner healing.

Beyond the private holiday, travelling offers immense benefits for teenagers. Firstly, it fosters self-reliance and adaptability. Navigating a new place, planning our trips, and reacting calmly to unforeseen circumstances develops crucial life skills that are indispensable for future success.

Secondly, travel acts as a great way to learn about the environment. Seeing the bleached coral or the floating plastic directly in the ocean turns an abstract concept like pollution into a truth we feel deep down. This first-hand exposure promotes a sense of urgency and encourages us to look after the planet better.

In conclusion, Pulau Redang remains my most cherished travel memory due to its natural beauty and the inner peace it provided. Ultimately, travel is the best education, fundamentally broadening our horizons and helping us become more global-minded and conscious individuals.
